runs.text: Nobody calls it Germany. Not even Germans. They say <<ˈ|d|ɔɪ|tʃ|l|ɑ|n|t>>, from an old word for: of the people. Austria is <<ˈ|ɜ|s|t|ə|r|aɪ|k>>. The eastern realm. Switzerland has four languages, so four names. On its coins, it's <<h|ɛ|l|ˈ|v|eɪ|ʃ|ə>>. That's why it's C. H. Hungary? <<ˈ|m|ɑ|dʒ|ɑ|r|ˌ|ɔ|r|s|ɑː|g>>. Land of the <<ˈ|m|æ|g|j|ɑ|r|z>>. Finland is <<ˈ|s|w|ɔ|m|i>>. Even the Finns aren't sure where that comes from. Greece is <<ˈ|h|ɛ|l|ə|s>>. Romans said <<ˈ|g|r|aɪ|k|i>>. Greeks call themselves <<ˈ|h|ɛ|l|iː|n|z>>. Albania is <<ʃ|tʃ|i|p|ə|ˈ|r|i|ɑ>>. Many link it to the eagle on its flag. Croatia? <<ˈ|h|ɜ|r|v|ɑ|t|s|k|ɑ>>. Montenegro is <<ˈ|t|s|ɜ|r|n|ɑ>> <<ˈ|g|ɔ|r|ɑ>>. Same meaning: black mountain. And Ireland is <<ˈ|ɛ|r|ə>>. Ireland literally means: land of <<ˈ|ɛ|r|ə>>. Which one surprised you? Part two is the Middle East. Until then, remember:
